question:
If the length of steel rod is 5cm longer than copper rod at all
temperatures. ($\alpha$ for copper $= 1.7 \times 10^{- 5}ºC^{- 1}$ and
$\alpha$ for steel $\left. \ = 1.1 \times 10^{- 5}C^{- 1} \right)$
option_1: Length of steel rod is 14.17cm and length of copper rod is 9.17cm
option_2: Length of steel rod is 15.17cm and length of copper rod is 6.17cm
option_3: Length of steel rod is 14.17cm and length of copper rod is 10.17cm
option_4: Length of steel rod is 15.17cm and length of copper rod is 9.17cm
solution:
$\mathcal{l}_{1}\left( 1 + \alpha_{1}\Delta T \right) - \mathcal{l}_{2}\left( 1 + \alpha_{2}\Delta T \right) = \mathcal{l}_{1} - \mathcal{l}_{2}$
$\mathcal{l}_{1}\alpha_{1}\Delta T = \mathcal{l}_{2}\alpha_{2}\Delta T$
$\mathcal{l}_{1}\alpha_{1} = \mathcal{l}_{2}\alpha_{2}$
$\Rightarrow \mathcal{l}_{1} \times 1.7 = \mathcal{l}_{2} \times 1.1$
$17\mathcal{l}_{1} = 11\mathcal{l}_{2}$
As $\left( \mathcal{l}_{2} - \mathcal{l}_{1} = 5 \right)$
$\Rightarrow 17\mathcal{l}_{2} - 11\mathcal{l}_{2} = 5 \times 17$
$6\mathcal{l}_{2} = 85$
$\Rightarrow \mathcal{l}_{2} = \frac{85}{6} = 14.17cm$
$\mathcal{l}_{1} = 9.17cm$

question:
In the fig. shown a cart moves on a smooth horizontal surface
due to an external constant force of magnitude F. The initial mass of
the cart is $M_{0}$and velocity is zero. Sand falls on to the cart with
negligible velocity at constant rate$\mu\ kg/s$ and sticks to the cart.

solution:
[IMAGE] Formula $F = m\frac{dv}{dt} + (V - u)\frac{dm}{dt}$
Here u=velocity of sand =0
$m = M_{o} - \mu t = mass\ at\ time\ t$
and$\frac{dm}{dt} = \mu$
$\therefore F = (M_{0} + \mu t)\frac{dm}{dt} + v\mu$
$(F - \mu v)dt = (M_{o} + \mu t)dv$
$\int_{0}^{t}\frac{dt}{M_{0} + \mu t} = \int_{0}^{v}\frac{dv}{F - \mu v}$
${\lbrack log(M_{0} + \mu t)\rbrack}_{0}^{t} = \frac{1}{\mu}\lbrack log(F - \mu v)\rbrack_{0}^{v}$
$log\frac{(M_{0} + \mu t)}{M_{0}} = log(\frac{F}{F - \mu v})$
$F - \mu v = \frac{M_{o}F}{M_{0} + \mu t} \Rightarrow v = \frac{Ft}{M_{0} + \mu t}$

Path of swimmer relative to ground is a straight line at 45º

On squaring$1 + 25\cos^{2}\theta + 10cos\theta = 25 - 25\cos^{2}\theta$
$50\cos^{2}\theta + 10cos\theta - 24 = 0$
On solving, we get$\theta = 53^{\circ}$

B at centre of a circle $= \frac{\mu_{0}I}{2R}$

question:

conveyer belt moving with constant velocityV. If the coefficient of
friction between the belt and sphere is$\frac{2}{7}$, the distance
travelled by the centre of the sphere before it starts pure rolling is.
solution:
Initial situation w.r.t. the conveyer belt:
$\mu mgR = \frac{2}{5}{mR}^{2} \cdot \alpha$ $\Rightarrow$
$\alpha = \frac{5}{7} \cdot \frac{g}{R}$
At pure rolling:
$v^{'} = v - (\mu g)t$and $\omega^{'} = 0 + \left( \frac{5}{7} \cdot \frac{g}{R} \right)t$

$S = \frac{v^{2}}{g} - \frac{v^{2}}{7g}$ (w.r.t. belt)

of$s_{b} = vt = v\left( \frac{v}{g} \right) = \frac{v^{2}}{g}$

question:
A thin walled hollow cylinder is closed from both the ends. The
mass of the curved part is m and the mass of each circular part is also
m. The radius of the cylinder is R and its length is 2R. What will be
the moment of inertia of this hollow cylinder about the axis,
perpendicular to its length and passing through its centre of mass?
solution:
First find I of the hollow tube
$I_{1} = \int\frac{{dmR}^{2}}{2} + \int_{x = - \frac{\mathcal{l}}{2}}^{x = + \frac{\mathcal{l}}{2}}{(\frac{m}{\mathcal{l}}dx)}x^{2}$
$I_{1} = \frac{{mR}^{2}}{2} + \frac{m^{\mathcal{l}^{2}}}{12}$ where
$\mathcal{l} = 2R$
So $I_{1} = \frac{5}{6}{mR}^{2}$
Now moment of inertias of each circular plate about that axis.
$I = \frac{mR^{2}}{4} + mR^{2} = \frac{5}{4}mR^{2}$
$I_{total} = \frac{5}{6}{mR}^{2} + 2 \times \left( \frac{5}{4}{mR}^{2} \right)$
$I_{total} = \frac{10}{3}{mR}^{2}$
subject: Physics

question:
A system undergoes three quasi-static processes sequentially as
indicated in the given figure. $1 \rightarrow 2$is an isobaric process,
$2 \rightarrow 3$ is a polytrophic process with
$\gamma = \frac{4}{3}$and $3 \rightarrow 1$ is a process in which PV=
constant.
$P_{2} = P_{1} = 4 \times 10^{5}Nm^{- 2},P_{3} = 1 \times 10^{5}Nm^{- 2}$and$\ V_{1} = 1m^{3}$.
The heat transfer of the cycle is $\Delta Q,$ change in internal
energy is $\Delta U$ and the work done is $\Delta W$. for polytropic
process $PV^{\gamma} =$ constant.
(Take $\mathcal{l}$n2 = 0.693). Then
solution:
For the process $3 \rightarrow 1$
$P_{1}V_{1} = P_{3}V_{3} \Rightarrow V_{3} = \frac{P_{1}V_{1}}{P_{3}} = \frac{4 \times 10^{5} \times 1}{1 \times 10^{5}} = 4m^{3}$
For the process $2 \rightarrow 3$
$P_{2}V_{2}^{\gamma} = P_{3}V_{3}^{\gamma} \Rightarrow V_{2} = \left( \frac{P_{3}}{P_{2}} \right)^{\frac{1}{\gamma}}V_{3} = 4\left( \frac{1}{4} \right)^{\frac{3}{4}} = 4^{\frac{1}{4}} = \sqrt{2}m^{3}$
For the process $1 \rightarrow 2$
$W_{12} = P_{1}\left( V_{2} - V_{1} \right) = \left( \sqrt{2} - 1 \right)4 \times 10^{5}J$
For the process $2 \rightarrow 3$
$W_{23} = \frac{\left( P_{2}V_{2} - P_{3}V_{3} \right)}{(\gamma - 1)} = 12(\sqrt{2} - 1) \times 10^{5}J$
For the process $3 \rightarrow 1$,
$w_{31} = - P_{1}V_{1}ln\frac{V_{3}}{V_{1}} - 4 \times 10^{5} \times 1 \times ln(4)$
For cyclic process, $\Delta\ U = 0$
$\therefore\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W = \Delta W = 4 \times 10^{5}(\sqrt{2} - 1)$
$1 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 3 \rightarrow 1$
$\Delta Q = + 12 \times 10^{5}(\sqrt{2} - 1) - 4 \times 10^{5} \times 2 \times 0.693$
$= 1.08 \times 10^{5}J$
subject: Physics

question:
A solid sphere of mass m and radius r is gently placed on a
conveyer belt moving with constant velocityV. If the coefficient of
friction between the belt and sphere is$\frac{2}{7}$, the distance
travelled by the centre of the sphere before it starts pure rolling is.
solution:
Initial situation w.r.t. the conveyer belt:
$\mu mgR = \frac{2}{5}{mR}^{2} \cdot \alpha$ $\Rightarrow$
$\alpha = \frac{5}{7} \cdot \frac{g}{R}$
At pure rolling:
$v^{'} = v - (\mu g)t$and $\omega^{'} = 0 + \left( \frac{5}{7} \cdot \frac{g}{R} \right)t$
(Since at pure rolling)
$\Rightarrow$ $v - \mu gt = \frac{5}{7} \cdot g \cdot t$
$\Rightarrow$ $t = \frac{v}{g}\left( \because\mu = \frac{2}{7} \right)$
For centre of the sphere:$S = v\left( \frac{v}{g} \right) - \frac{1}{2} \cdot \left( \frac{2}{7} \cdot g \right)\left( \frac{v^{2}}{g^{2}} \right)$
$S = \frac{v^{2}}{g} - \frac{v^{2}}{7g}$ (w.r.t. belt)
In this time, the belt with speed will move a distance
of$s_{b} = vt = v\left( \frac{v}{g} \right) = \frac{v^{2}}{g}$
[IMAGE] Distance travelled w.r.t. ground will be:$S_{g} = \left| S - S_{b} \right| = \left| \left( \frac{v^{2}}{g} - \frac{v^{2}}{7g} \right) - \left( \frac{v^{2}}{g} \right) \right| = \frac{v^{2}}{7g}$

question:
A particle of mass $m = \frac{5}{42}kg$ is tied to an end of an
inextensible string and is whirled in a vertical circle as shown below.
Then, the difference in tension of string at A and B i.e.
$T_{A} - T_{B}$ in Newton is: (particle completes the circle)
solution:
$\Delta T = \frac{3mg\Delta h}{I}$
$h_{B} - h_{A} = I(\frac{3}{5} + \frac{4}{5}) = \frac{7I}{5}$
$T_{A} - B_{B} = \frac{3mg}{I}(h_{B} - h_{A})$
$= \frac{3mg}{I} \times \frac{7I}{5}$
$= \frac{21mg}{5} = \frac{21}{5} \times \frac{5}{42} \times 10$
$= 5N$
subject: Physics
